question.text: An <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>L</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>.</mo></math> circuit contains resistance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>110</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mi></mi></math> and a supply of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>220</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>300</mn><mo> </mo><mi>rad</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> angular frequency. If only capacitance is removed from the circuit, current lags behind the voltage by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>45</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. If on the other hand, the only the inductor is removed the current leads by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>45</mn><mo>°</mo></math> with the applied voltage.
